summary.decisions: Stun check placed after the death pipeline so dying enemies ignore stun; timer decremented before the ai() skip so the frame that drives it to 0 is still a stun frame (clean one-frame-later resume); no state save/restore needed since aiState is never mutated during stun.
summary.lessons_learned: Boundary semantics matter: with hitstunTimer = N*DT, ai() resumes on step N+1, not N — test asserts this explicitly. The bck/ test dir contains archived bit-roted tests (bad import paths) that fail standalone but are excluded from run-all.mjs; don't treat those as regressions.
summary.tradeoffs: Plain countdown field instead of a unified Timers entry — consistent with existing hitFlash and required because applyKnockback (task 1.1) writes victim.hitstunTimer from outside; clamped at 0 to avoid negative drift.
summary.done: Added hitstunTimer (seconds) + stunned getter to Enemy; update() now skips ai() while stunned but still integrates gravity/vx/vy so knockback plays out visibly; aiState is untouched during stun so the enemy resumes its exact prior AI state on expiry. hitFlash visual unchanged. Added js/test/enemyHitstun.test.js (9 cases): ai() frozen during window, physics integrate (horizontal shove + gravity), resume of prior state, boundary frame behavior, dead-enemy precedence.
